facts.why: The menu prices everything in cents. Australia used pounds, shillings and pence in 1959 and went decimal on 14 February 1966. The film itself prices a dress in guineas.
facts.fix: Reprice in shillings and pence: 3/6 for the platter, 3/- for the egg sandwiches, 8/6 for the paprikash, 4/- for the cake and 2/6 for the punch.

facts.text: For Lisa, who was Lesley until this summer.
facts.why: Wikipedia spells the character Leslie ("Leslie 'Lisa' Miles").
facts.fix: For Lisa, who was Leslie until this summer.

facts.why: The plot only places the story in Goode's department store. A tea room is not mentioned in the sources opened.

vibe.verdict: A handsome 1959 tea room, but decimal cents break the period and the film's dress, Patty's nightdress and Magda's party get no look in.
missing: Lisa's dress marked down from 150 to 75, 50 and finally 35 guineas
Magda's New Year's Eve party at her house
Rudi buying an apartment and proposing to Fay
Magda planning her own fashion shop
ideas: Reprice every dish in shillings and pence.
Swap "Model Gowns poppy seed cake" for "Guinea dress cake", priced 35 guineas as a joke.
Swap the egg sandwiches for "Patty's pink nightdress pink iced fancies".
Add a "New Year's Eve at Magda's" place card.
